$comment: P64 [[D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL-PE-OVERALIGN]] (static twin), the NEGATIVE half: a statically allocated object over-aligned beyond what the OUTPUT FORMAT can ENCODE is refused BY NAME, never placed misaligned. $$ THIS ENTRY MOVED FROM 8192 TO 16384 IN P64, BECAUSE AT 8192 IT PINNED A DIVERGENCE AS THE CONTRACT. MEASURED, each PE reference probed SEPARATELY, BUILD **and** RUN with the runtime address asserted on a multi-object subject: mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 19.51 BOTH return 42 at 8192 (MSVC needs `/link /ALIGN:8192`), so the old boundary refused what two working references run. `pe::encodeExec` now PLACES an 8192 static by padding within the section, exactly as `ld` does -- see `examples/c/alignment_overaligned_static_placed`, the positive witness -- and this entry sits at the first value BOTH references refuse by name, quoted from a run on THIS FILE rather than paraphrased: gcc gives the TYPE-decorated form here, "error: alignment of 'g1' is greater than maximum object file alignment 8192" (the VARIABLE-decorated spelling gives "requested alignment '16384' exceeds object file maximum 8192" -- two messages, one number), and MSVC 19.51, probed in its own `__declspec(align(16384))` spelling because it casts no vote in a foreign one, gives `error C2345: align(16384): illegal alignment value`. 16384 is one step past what PE/COFF's FOUR-BIT IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_* field can hold, which is why both land there independently. $$ MEASURED in P63 with the requestable ceiling raised and no gate at all: the same shape built rc 0 on pe64 and the FIRST over-aligned static failed its own `%` check at run time (exit 50) -- a clean build with a misplaced object, the silent miscompile this gate exists to prevent. A single over-aligned object at the head of a section can be right BY LUCK, which is why the program carries two behind odd-sized fillers. $$ THE CONTROLS ARE WHAT MAKE IT A STATEMENT ABOUT STORAGE RATHER THAN ABOUT ALIGNMENT: the SAME mingw compiler at the SAME value BUILDS AND RUNS the request on a TYPE and on an AUTOMATIC object (MEASURED, exit 42 for both at 16384 and 65536). So this ceiling belongs to the format writer and must never move into the semantic ladder, where it would refuse `aligned(65536)` types every reference runs. $ THE BOUND IS NOW WHAT THE CONTAINER CAN HOLD, not the format document's `optionalHeader.sectionAlignment` -- that old bound was refuted twice over: it refused a value both references run, and its remedy was wrong, since `ld` leaves SectionAlignment at 0x1000 and pads WITHIN the section. $ PE ONLY, and that is measured rather than conservative: on `elf64-x86_64-linux-exec` the identical program places its objects correctly at 8192, 16384 and 65536 (run under WSL, exit 42), so an ELF gate would refuse what DSS demonstrably gets right. `positioned: false` because a link-tier diagnostic carries no source span.
